author: Nicholas Sorensen
title: Breast cancer and heart attack survivor wins over $2 million from Pennsylvania Lottery - NewsBreak
text: A Warren County grandmother who has survived breast cancer and a heart attack received a pleasant surprise when she won over $2 million playing an online game from the Pennsylvania Lottery . Warren County resident Nicole Walter was presented a check for $2,021,096 from the Pennsylvania Lottery on Aug. 13 at the Western Pennsylvania Lottery office in Millcreek at 4802 Pittsburgh Ave. The winnings come after Walter hit the jackpot on the online game Monopoly Progressive Jackpots. The total amount is the largest internet instant prize won from the Monopoly-themed online Pennsylvania Lottery game, said Victoria Holan, western Pa. regional sales manager for the lottery. For Walter, the money is not only life-changing but gives her a sense of relief following some recent health battles. "Starting in 2023 I had ankle surgery and they found that I had breast cancer, so that’s where the process started," Walter said. "That November I had breast cancer surgery and they took all my lymph nodes. That was a healing battle between the ankle and breast cancer, so I wasn’t able to go back to work. The radiation later caused a heart attack." The health battles mixed in with other daily expenses caused some financial stress on Walter, 42. That stress soon was relieved after she played Monopoly Progressive Jackpots online on Aug. 2. A winner in June: Meet Gary Winner, who cashed in more than $1 million from a Pennsylvania Lottery ticket "My fiancé (Steven Haight) and I were playing (on phones), sitting side by side," Walter said. "As I was hitting it, the bonus popped up and it went blank. We wondered what happened and here it popped up that it was a mega bonus with over $2 million. It was awesome." Pennsylvania Lottery officials said that the prize amount was one of the largest jackpots won by anyone near the Erie County area. Walter and her fiancé, as of the morning of Aug. 13, are continuing to consult with their accountant on what steps to take next. It didn't take them long though to start spending some of their winnings on themselves. So far, Walter and Haight have purchased two vehicles and plan on investing in rental properties to keep earning more income. They also plan to help their 10 grandchildren with setting up accounts for their futures. Earlier this year Walter had to cancel her insurance due to the finacial stress. The winnings helped her invest back into insurance. "It is very lifechanging and mind blowing," Walter said. "To go from stressed out and tired; so it could have never come at a better time." As Walter explained, they are aiming to be responsible with their winnings. Her and Haight said that they did not put a lot of money into the game despite winning big. "We heard from the winners; playing responsible is key," said Diana Dietz, communications director for the Pennsylvania Lottery. "Have fun, and in this case they won big and have big plans, and they are being responsible with their plans for their prize. That’s always something we encourage, too." Contact Nicholas Sorensen at Nsorensen@gannett.com . This article originally appeared on Erie Times-News: Breast cancer and heart attack survivor wins over $2 million from Pennsylvania Lottery
